title: Извинения Макса за ревность  (Max Apologizes for His Jealousy)

segments.t: At the restaurant bar, Max finds Kostya looking exhausted and sincerely apologizes for his jealous outburst over Ilya the previous evening. Racked with guilt, Kostya pours Max a stiff drink and claims he saw nothing unusual with Sasha.
Костян, ты что, спишь, что ли?
Слушай, Кость, ты извини за вчерашнюю, ладно?
Я не хотел, чтоб с Ильёй так...
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
Костян, ты что, спишь, что ли?
'Kostyan, what, are you asleep on your feet?' Max raises the pitch on 'really' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Kostya answers right away.
Слушай, Кость, ты извини за вчерашнюю, ладно?
'Listen, Kostya, I am sorry about last night, okay?' The grammar packs 'listen' and 'really?!' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Я не хотел, чтоб с Ильёй так...
'I did not mean for things with Ilya to turn out like that...' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'like this' in spoken Russian.
'Yeah, everything is totally fine.' The grammar packs 'yes' and 'fine' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Kostya answers right away.
'Here, this is for you.' The grammar packs 'there you go' and 'you' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Max, do not get upset.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'be upset' to negate the statement.
'I mean, just drink it.' The meaning hinges on 'sense' working together with 'drink' in spoken Russian. Kostya answers right away.
'Ah, thank you.' Notice how Russian expresses 'and' and 'thank you' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'And how is Sasha doing over there?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'Sasha'.
'I did not see anything at all.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'saw' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Kostya answers right away.
'What do you mean...' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'sense' before landing on 'sense'.
'Well, just like that.' The grammar packs 'come on' and 'like this' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Listen to me, Max.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'listen' and finishing on 'Max'. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Костян, ты что, спишь, что ли?
Слушай, Кость, ты извини за вчерашнюю, ладно?
Я не хотел, чтоб с Ильёй так...
